learning_outcomes.text: Learning single-variable functions, limit, continuity, and derivative concepts and applying them to engineering problems.
Analyzing physical and engineering systems using differential calculus methods.
Examining function graphs, interpreting rates of change, and solving optimization problems.
Performing calculations for area, volume, and engineering applications using the integral concept and basic integration techniques.
Developing mathematical thinking, problem-solving, and analytical analysis skills to form a basis for mechanical engineering courses.

syllabus_topics: Sets. Number Sets. Equations. Identities. Inequalities.
Function concept. Properties of functions (one-to-one, onto, etc.)
Trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, and hyperbolic functions. Piecewise functions, specially defined functions (Absolute value, floor, sign functions)
Limit concept and limit calculation with limit definition. Proof of rules used for limit calculation. Sandwich theorem. Limits of trigonometric functions.
Right and left-hand limits. Indeterminate forms (0/0, infinity/infinity, 0.infinity, infinity-infinity, 1^infinity)
Continuity concept in functions. Types of discontinuity. Properties of continuous functions (Intermediate Value Theorem, absolute maximum and minimum, local maximum and minimum definitions, ...)
Derivative concept and derivative calculation with derivative definition. Proof of differentiation rules with derivative definition. Derivative of inverse function.
Higher-order derivatives. Derivatives of functions given by parametric equations. Derivatives of implicit functions.
Tangent and normal equations. Increasing and decreasing functions.
Differential Concept and approximate calculation. Indeterminate forms (Examination of 8 indeterminate forms with L'Hopital's Rule).
Maximum and minimum of functions, asymptotes
Engineering problems. Approximate calculation with differential. Series expansions
assessment_rules: The midterm exam accounts for 40% of the final grade, and the final exam accounts for 60%. Midterm and final exam dates are determined by the University Senate and specified in the academic calendar.
